Subject: Discovery notes + next step options

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick write-up of what I took away and two possible next steps so we can pick what makes sense for Novus:

Key notes from call:
- Primary goal: reduce inference latency for search/checkout recommendations from ~350ms to <120ms for 99th percentile.
- Workloads: mixed short prompt generation for recommenders, periodic batch embeddings for catalog sync.
- Data sensitivity: PII redaction required, will need VPC/private deploy for regulated markets.
- Current infra: in-house GPU pool + AWS for inference; estimated spend ~ $12k/month.

Suggested next steps (pick one):
1) 6-week pilot (recommended): Dedicated pool + prefix caching + lightweight evals on your sample traffic. We scope success metrics (latency, cost per 1k tokens) and roll a canary in staging. Deliverable: pilot report + recommended config.
2) Proof-of-concept (30-day): Quick hosted test to validate latency and token-cost profile, lower commitment.

Attachment: 2027-03-04-Discovery-Notes-Redwood-20270304.pdf (2 pages) — short summary + proposed pilot outline.

If you think there's fit, which option feels most useful to you? If not a fit, any frank feedback helps — e.g., priority, technical blockers, or procurement timing.

If easier, I can book 15 minutes to walk the pilot plan through with your infra lead.

Thanks,
Logan
